title: Amazon
summary: Problems whose patterns are commonly reported in Amazon coding interviews, from Easy to Hard. Approximate and hand curated, not an official or verified question list.
lesson:
About this list
- Each problem practices a pattern that candidates commonly describe from Amazon technical loops: prefix search and autocomplete, heaps and top-k selection, multi-source grid BFS, greedy scheduling, caches, intervals, trees, and sliding windows.
- Problems are grouped Easy, Medium, and Hard so you can warm up on core array and hashing mechanics before practicing search, graph, and streaming problems.
- The selection is approximate. Interview rounds vary by organization and role, so treat this track as pattern practice rather than a prediction of what you will be asked.

What to expect
- Candidates often report practical problem framings around catalogs, fulfillment grids, scheduling, and caching where clarifying requirements and edge cases upfront is essential.
- Follow-ups frequently probe scalability: handling large catalogs with tries or sorted ranges, bounding memory with heaps or caches, and avoiding quadratic scans.
- Clean decomposition into readable helper methods and explicit complexity trade-offs are commonly emphasized alongside correctness.

How to prepare
- Start each problem by clarifying tie-breaking, mutability of inputs, and empty or unmatched cases.
- Practice choosing between sorting + two pointers, heaps, and tries based on whether queries are one-shot or repeated.
- After passing, review how your solution behaves under skewed inputs and large scale.
